user.title: Network Fault Locator
user.description: Watches the path from Home Assistant to your router, chosen local devices, ISP and the internet, and tells where a problem is.

data.name: Name
data.notify_entity: Notify when an incident is resolved

data_description.name: Name of the device.
data_description.router: IP of your main router (pre-filled with the first hop Home Assistant sees).
data_description.internet_targets: Public IPs that answer pings (up to 5). The first one is also used for the traceroute.
data_description.dns_host: A hostname that should always resolve.
data_description.notify_entity: Optional notify entity (e.g. Telegram or mobile app) for the incident summary.

devices.title: Local devices to watch
devices.description: Pick the devices on your network to watch, e.g. mesh access points, extenders or switches. The list comes from what Home Assistant already knows about your network (nothing is scanned). To add one that isn't listed, type 'Name=IP' or just the IP and press Enter. Up to 30; you can leave it empty.

data_description.devices: A problem reaching these is reported as a local device issue, separately from the router and the ISP.

error.invalid_host: Not a valid unicast IP address or hostname.
error.invalid_device: Use 'Name=IP' or just an IP address / hostname, with unique names.
error.no_targets: Add at least one internet target.
error.check_too_long: Too short for this many pings: an unreachable host takes about 1 s per ping. Increase the interval or lower the pings per check.

abort.no_icmp: Home Assistant is not allowed to send ICMP pings on this system.

data.notify_entity: Notify when an incident is resolved

data_description.router: IP of your main router (pre-filled with the first hop Home Assistant sees).
data_description.internet_targets: Public IPs that answer pings (up to 5). The first one is also used for the traceroute.
data_description.dns_host: A hostname that should always resolve.
data_description.notify_entity: Optional notify entity (e.g. Telegram or mobile app) for the incident summary.
data_description.ping_count: Packets sent to each target per check.
data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between checks. Must be longer than the pings per check (in seconds) + 3.
data_description.loss_window: Packet loss is pooled over this many minutes.
data_description.loss_threshold: Loss (in percentage points above the loss to the router) that counts as a problem.
data_description.min_incident: Shorter incidents fire no 'resolved' event or notification.
